affectedSurfaces: Codex native CLI passive-session launch boundary
hypothesis: Declaring passive mode unsupported for the Codex native harness and rejecting it both during generic readiness routing and at the adapter boundary prevents a nominally read-only session from reaching native shell, network, or extension effects that KOTA cannot classify or deny.

metricsCompared.name: passive native-effect launch paths
metricsCompared.baseline: Passive Codex runs removed writable roots but still launched the native runtime for shell execution, outbound GET and POST requests, and native MCP/tool calls.
metricsCompared.candidate: All four covered effect classes are rejected before harness hooks, sandbox setup, or subprocess launch.

metricsCompared.name: focused passive-boundary regression suite
metricsCompared.baseline: The adapter regression expected passive mode to launch with an empty writable-root set, and the generic runner had no passive incompatibility declaration to enforce.
metricsCompared.candidate: Five focused files and 53 tests pass, including generic pre-hook rejection and adapter-level shell, GET, POST, and native-tool launch denials.

rationale: This is a fail-closed repair for a confirmed high-severity authorization bypass. The native Codex harness cannot mediate individual tool effects, so rejecting passive mode preserves KOTA's read-only contract instead of presenting an unenforced policy. The generic readiness boundary and direct adapter boundary both reject before execution, focused regressions cover the cited effect classes, and typecheck, build, strict-type, layout, and formatting validation pass.
